title: Next Greater Element II
description:
Given a circular integer array `nums` (meaning the element immediately after `nums[nums.length - 1]` is `nums[0]`), return an array `result` of the same length where `result[i]` is the **next greater number** for `nums[i]`.

The next greater number of `nums[i]` is the first element strictly greater than `nums[i]` encountered when traversing forward from index `i` in circular order (wrapping around from the end of the array back to index `0`). If no such strictly greater element exists in the entire array, set `result[i]` to `-1`.
hints: Simulate the circular array by conceptually iterating through the array twice (`0` to `2n - 1`) using modulo indexing `i % n`.
Maintain a monotonic decreasing stack of indices whose next greater element has not yet been found.
When the current element `nums[i % n]` is strictly greater than `nums[stack[-1]]`, pop from the stack and record `nums[i % n]` as its answer. Only push indices during the first pass (`i < n`).

examples.explanation: For nums[0] = 1, the next greater element is 2. For nums[1] = 2, no greater element exists (-1). For nums[2] = 1, wrapping around yields 2.
Each element finds the next strictly larger value clockwise; 4 is the maximum so its answer is -1, while the trailing 3 wraps around to 4.
5 has no greater element (-1). Every other element wraps around the circular array to reach 5.
